subject: Food Science
title: Titanium Dioxide Ban
description: A 60-second lesson on Titanium Dioxide Ban.

hook.text: Titanium dioxide made Oreo filling white and Skittles shiny. The EU banned it in 2022. The US still allows it.

buildup.text: TiO₂ (E171) is a whitening agent used in candy, frosting, chewing gum, and thousands of products.

discovery.text: EFSA concluded in 2021 that TiO₂ nanoparticles could damage DNA. They couldn't establish a safe daily intake.

twist.text: The FDA reviewed the same evidence and kept TiO₂ approved—citing different risk assessment methodologies.

climax.text: Mars removed TiO₂ from Skittles in Europe but kept it in US Skittles. Same candy, different safety standards.

punchline.text: Banned in Paris. Legal in New York. Same molecule, different verdict.

quiz.question: Why did the EU ban titanium dioxide in food?
options: EFSA found nanoparticles could damage DNA with no safe daily intake established
